qAndA.answer: He tared the balance once to zero it out and then again with the weighing bottle on it to account for the weight of the bottle itself.
qAndA.question: Why did the scientist tare the balance twice?

qAndA.answer: The waste beaker was used to collect any excess solid that was removed from the weighing bottle to ensure an accurate weight.
qAndA.question: What was the purpose of the waste beaker?

qAndA.answer: He tapped the weighing bottle and visually checked to confirm no solid remained.
qAndA.question: How did the scientist ensure that all the solid was transferred to the clean beaker?

qAndA.answer: He subtracted the 'mass of weighing bottle & residue' from the 'mass of weighing bottle & sample'.
qAndA.question: What calculation did the scientist use to determine the "mass of solid used"?

activities.description: Scientist closes the weighing balance doors and tares the balance.
He places the weighing bottle on the balance and tares it again.
Scientist fills the weighing bottle with the solid using a spatula.
He checks the weight, removes excess solid, and ensures the desired weight is achieved.
Scientist removes the weighing bottle from the balance.
He transfers the solid into a clean beaker.
Scientist places the empty weighing bottle back onto the balance.
He records the reading as the 'mass of weighing bottle & residue' and explains its significance.
Scientist transfers the remaining solid from the weighing bottle to the clean beaker.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In this lesson, you'll be learning the wing by different technique.
Into this technique, we are going to weigh 5 grams of the solid.
So far are the apparatus that you need.
A wing balance, a waist-bigger, a clean beaker,
a wing bottle that is clean and dry, and a clean spatula.
First, ensure that all the windows are closed and care the wing balance.
Next, put the wing bottle in and tap.
Next, we'll fill the wing bottle with the solid.
If you have exceeded the weights that you need,
take out the wing bottle and dispose any unwanted solid into the waist-bigger.
Once you have reached the weight that you want,
take out the wing bottle,
close the window of the wing balance and tap.
After that, put back the wing bottle with the solid in
and take the reading of the wing balance.
This reading would be the mass of the wing bottle and sample that you need to record in your
lead report.
After you are done,
transfer the solid from the wing bottle into the clean beaker.
Make sure you tap the wing bottle to transfer all the solid into the beaker.
After this is done, tear the wing balance again.
Place the wing bottle back into the wing balance.
The reading that you see on the wing balance would be the mass of the wing bottle and
residue, and you will need to record this reading in your lead report.
After this is done, subtract the second reading from the first reading,
and the value that you get would be the mass of solid use in the experiment.
